findings.body:
**Assert that sibling replay retains exactly one decision.**

Both assertions check the triage row status. If the second harvest publishes another decision for the sibling, the row can still say `needs-human` and the test will pass. Assert that recovery retains one decision for the sibling, then check that the next harvest leaves the same event ID and count.
findings.title: Assert that sibling replay retains exactly one decision.

findings.body:
**Assert the operation name and message in the usage artifact.**

The test accepts an `error` object with only `kind` and `exitCode`. The stderr assertion does not check what a JSON consumer receives. Assert the expected `subcommand` and a nonempty `message` in stdout. As per coding guidelines, I1 requires a usage error object with `kind`, `subcommand`, `message`, and `exitCode`.
findings.title: Assert the operation name and message in the usage artifact.

findings.body:
**Read the current run record after recovery preparation.**

If preparation replaces `old-run` with a stale record, `original` still points to the queued record. Both assertions pass even though the queue would skip the sibling. Look up `old-run` again after `prepare_current_job` and assert its state and job list.
findings.title: Read the current run record after recovery preparation.

findings.body:
**Check that the detector failure leaves the persisted run retryable.**

If `harvest` replaces the run record, saves it as failed, and re-raises `DetectorUnavailable`, the captured `record` still says `queued`. Check the current queue entry and reload the persisted queue to confirm that the next tick still sees a queued run.
findings.title: Check that the detector failure leaves the persisted run retryable.

findings.body:
**Assert the scanner’s `+` prefix on every instruction line.**

If the U+0085-separated line is rendered as ` third` instead of `+third`, `line[1:]` produces `third` in both cases. The test passes, but `secret_scan_diff` skips the line with a space prefix. Compare the full hunk lines with the expected `+`-prefixed lines.
findings.title: Assert the scanner’s `+` prefix on every instruction line.

findings.body:
**Clear caller `GIT_*` overrides in the real-Git recovery subtest.**

`crq.run` and `crq.git` pass `env=None` to `subprocess.run` (`apps/crq-python/crq.py:124-134`), so these calls inherit the test process environment. The `git_process` wrapper at `apps/crq-python/test_review_admission_execution.py:232-235` forwards the environment unchanged. If the process exports `GIT_DIR`, for example when it runs from a Git hook, `git rev-parse` in the `partial` clone reads the caller's repository instead. The head imported at line 268 is absent from that repository, so the recovery at line 273 leaves the item pending and the assertion at line 274 fails.

Clear the `GIT_*` variables for this subtest, as the planner test already does at lines 404-410, so recovery Git calls use only the `partial` clone.
findings.title: Clear caller `GIT` overrides in the real-Git recovery subtest.

findings.body:
**Isolate the real-commit fixture from the caller’s Git configuration.**

The test can fail before it reaches `verify_source_scripts`. With `commit.gpgSign=true` and no key for the fixture identity, Git tries to sign the commit. `--no-verify` does not disable signing or skip a configured `prepare-commit-msg` hook. Inherited repository variables such as `GIT_DIR` can also redirect the commands outside the temporary repository. Use a controlled Git environment for fixture setup and verification. Keep the real commit, but disable signing and hooks for the fixture. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Isolate the real-commit fixture from the caller’s Git configuration.

findings.body:
**Check that the images directory is locked during the fetch.**

This assertion only checks the last `flock` flag. The test also passes if `fetch_image` takes the lock after `_fetch_image_locked` returns or locks a different file. Check inside the fetch callback that an exclusive lock has already been acquired on the images directory and has not been released.
findings.title: Check that the images directory is locked during the fetch.

findings.body:
**Keep the query successful when testing unsettled jobs.**

This fixture sets `settled=False` and removes `query_ok`. A verifier that checks `query_ok` but ignores `settled` still passes the test. Keep `query_ok=True` and `rc=0` with the running job so that the unsettled result alone must prevent proof.
findings.title: Keep the query successful when testing unsettled jobs.

findings.body:
**Test each post-boundary activation refusal independently.**

The fixture permits direct activation after manager restart and dependency activation after reboot in the same case. A verifier that ignores the reboot refusal still returns `mask_persisted=False` because of the manager result. Start each case with both boundaries valid, then make one activation succeed and assert that it defeats `mask_persisted`.
findings.title: Test each post-boundary activation refusal independently.

findings.body:
**Require the expected check keys before checking their values.**

If `build_checks` drops `timer_state_after_reboot`, this loop never reaches its assertion and the test still passes. Assert the expected key set before iterating so the positive fixture detects missing results as well as incorrect values.
findings.title: Require the expected check keys before checking their values.

findings.body:
**Make the download match the stale manifest only.**

`b"unexpected"` matches neither fixture digest. A verifier that refreshes the manifest but still accepts an image that matches the stale digest passes this test and the positive refresh test. Put the hash of `b"unexpected"` in the stale manifest and keep a different digest in the refreshed manifest. The test will then distinguish rejection under the refreshed manifest from acceptance under the stale one.
findings.title: Make the download match the stale manifest only.

findings.body:
**Set the cleanup guard before the source check.**

`skip_cleanup` stays `False` until line 1381. A source mismatch raised by `verify_source_scripts` at lines 1361-1362 therefore reaches the `except` block with `skip_cleanup` still `False` and `launched` still `None`. That block calls `stop_owned_process(run, purge=False, launched=None)`, which skips the identity guard and dispatches `_stop_owned_process` directly. The comment at `vm-feasibility.py:1376-1377` says that a refusal before the lock must not stop another invocation's VM. This path breaks that rule. If another invocation can hold the same run path, the stop can terminate its guest.

The assertion at `test_vm_feasibility.py:847` expects that stop call on the source-mismatch path, so the test locks in the same behavior. Arm `skip_cleanup` at the start of the `try` block and assert that no stop occurs.

```diff
     try:
+        # Until the lock is held and the live check has passed, this invocation
+        # owns no guest: a busy lock or a refusal must not stop another's VM.
+        skip_cleanup = True
         run_dir = pathlib.Path(run["path"])
```

```diff
         stamp = host_stamp()
-        # Until the lock is held and the live check has passed, this invocation
-        # owns no guest: a busy lock or a refusal must not stop another's VM.
-        skip_cleanup = True
         with run_lock(pathlib.Path(run["path"])):
```

```diff
-            stop.assert_called_once()
+            stop.assert_not_called()
```
findings.title: Set the cleanup guard before the source check.
